sentences.text: This writ petition has been filed seeking issuance of a writ of mandamus directing the respondents to consider the representation made by the petitioner dated 03.11.2023 wherein the petitioner is seeking for payment of compensation in respect of the subject property measuring 1.48 acres in Survey No.235/8, Sholinganallur Village, Now Sholinganallur Taluk, Kancheepuram District.

2. Heard Mr.N.K.Sivakumar, learned counsel for petitioner, Mr.M.R.Gokulkrishnan, learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for respondents 1 and 3 and Mr.A.M.Ravindranath Jeyapal, learned Standing Counsel appearing for second respondent.
3. When the matter came up for hearing on 05.02.2025, this https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 07/03/2025 12:30:03 pm ) Writ Petition No.25617 of 2024 Court passed the following order:
"The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the second respondent seeks for some time to file a counter in this case.
2. The third respondent has already filed a counter in this case wherein the following stand has been taken:
"It is respectfully submitted that the Notice under Section 9(3) and 10 of the L.A.Act were served by procedure.
But no one turned up for enquiry.
There are no structures or trees etc.

As such, there is dispute in the ownership and hence entire compensation amount in respect of the land belonging to the survey No.235/8A1,
extent 1.90 acres for an award amount Rs.1,57,200/- was deposited in the civil court deposit U/S 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act.

The Notice under Section 9(3)
and 10 of the L.A.Act were served on the individual, during the award enquiry, she presented a petition stating that she is not willing to dispose the land.
There are no structures or trees in the land.
She is the absolute owner of the land.

Hence the entire compensation in respect of land belonging to the survey No.235/8A3 extent 0.06 Acre, 235/8A4 extent 0.14 Acres of land for an award amount of Rs.16,547/- is ordered to be paid to Tmt.Rani, W/O Krishnamurthy.
The compensation award was deposited in the revenue deposit in the Sub-Treasury, Saidapet.

Further, it is submitted that the details of the land owners/interested persons for the subject land as per the land acquisition proceedings are as follows :

The physical possession of the land was already taken by the Government and handed over to the Tamil Nadu Housing Board on 19.7.1994."

5. When the matter was taken up for hearing today, learned Additional Government Pleader appearing on behalf of respondents produced the original records.

On going through the same, it is seen that the communication was addressed to the Sub Judge, Poonamallee, on 31.01.1994, stating that a sum of Rs.1,57,200/- being the compensation amount payable for an extent of 1.90 acres was ordered to be kept in CCD and a reference under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1984, was made to the Court since the claimants did not prove their ownership.
In the said communication, the names of the interested persons were also mentioned.

The amount was sent to the Sub Court by means of a demand draft dated 29.12.1993 drawn at State Bank of India, Saidapet Branch, bearing No.358851.
6.
Apart from the above, a sum of Rs.16,547/- has been kept in revenue deposit and the original challan dated 10.05.1994 was also placed before this Court.
Even in that challan, there is a specific reference to the Award No.1 of 1993, dated 15.06.1993.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 07/03/2025 12:30:03 pm ) Writ Petition No.25617 of 2024 7.

In view of the above, there shall be a direction to the Sub Judge, Poonamallee, to act upon the communication dated 31.01.1994 made by the third respondent whereby a sum of Rs.1,57,200/- was deposited and assign a LAOP number for the same.
Notice shall be issued to the parties and final orders shall be passed within a period of six (6) months thereafter.
It is left open to the petitioner to establish his right before the concerned reference Court.
Depending upon the final result in the LAOP proceedings, the compensation payable to the petitioner can be ascertained.
If the petitioner is successful in getting compensation before the LAOP Court, he can also seek for his claim on the compensation that has been kept in the revenue deposit.
This writ petition is disposed of in the above terms.
No costs.
